name: S-KBD67
tagline: A Nerf blaster rebuilt as a first-person-shooter controller.
problem: Shooter games are played with a mouse and keyboard; the physical fantasy of actually aiming a blaster is missing.
solution: Microcontrollers, a gyroscope, a joystick and buttons mounted on the blaster stream motion and inputs over Wi-Fi as UDP packets to a Python app that maps them to mouse and keyboard events.
demo_moment: Pick up the toy gun, aim, pump to reload, pull the trigger — and the game on screen responds.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Gives an object every judge recognizes a job it was never meant for; the idea fits in one sentence.
Split into hardware and backend sub-teams that integrated at the end, keeping both halves moving in parallel.
No AI at a 2025 AI-heavy event; wow came from physical play, not model calls.
Organizer featured it as the lead past project on the next year's homepage.

lessons: A finished, playable toy beats an unfinished platform. Parallelize hardware and software from hour one.
